cells.tense: The picture arriving now is arriving whole, and you are here with it.
cells.act: move toward the thing you want, one step, today
cells.ask: Take one real step toward the thing you keep circling — a call, a draft, a booking — and do it before you've worked out whether it's sensible.
cells.core: What you picture these days comes out of what you've already lived through, not out of the mood of the hour. You imagine something and it holds up against the day. That steadiness is doing you good here, in the place where you let things go on purpose and something underneath gets shown. So when the pull is toward the next piece of what you want, let the step be small and unglamorous. What stops you isn't a shortage of ideas. It's the old habit of treating your own pictures as if they had to stand for other people before they counted. They don't. Say the shape of it to one person who asked, and feel the difference between saying it and losing it. Then move, while the picture is still warm in your hands.
cells.sheetLine: Say what you're picturing, then take one step today.
cells.verb: moving through uncertainty with just enough light for the next step
cells.place: where letting go clears room and shows what's underneath

cells.tense: A future is being carried around before it has been allowed to form.
cells.act: tend it small and ask nothing of it
cells.ask: Pick the smallest piece of what you're carrying and tend just that — five minutes, no plan, no purpose — then set it down without checking what it produced.
cells.core: You're bracing against outcomes, rehearsing them until they feel settled. The pictures run further out than the thing itself, and lately they've drifted from what's actually true for you or for anyone involved. The bright ones go very bright; the dark ones very dark. Both are out past the day they describe. This is the same imagining that usually serves you, gone past its edge — where you let go, you've started gripping harder instead, holding images the way you'd hold a plan. Nothing needs fixing by tonight. Not a new plan, not a better picture. Take the one small piece that's forming, five minutes, no plan, no need to see what comes of it. Then put it down. The next piece shows up when it's ready, not on the day you decided.
cells.sheetLine: Put the future down. Tend the small thing first.

cells.tense: You are still standing at a door you have already walked through.
cells.act: sit with not knowing for ten minutes instead of filling it
cells.ask: For ten quiet minutes today, don't reach for the answer; sit with the thing you don't know yet, deciding nothing, and let whatever comes pass through.
cells.core: The dream here is that there isn't one. Not that you lack the knack — the part of you that reads images has been shut for business, and you've been getting away with it. Every question about your day arrives with an answer already attached. Every picture is checked before it gets in, and comes back cleared or thrown out. That's real work, and it's tiring. Carrying on as if the picture were the problem keeps the whole thing complicated. What hasn't changed is the not-knowing, and you can let it sit for ten minutes without fixing it. Ten minutes isn't a project. It's standing still long enough to hear the first thing that showed up, before the reasons arrive and close the door.
cells.sheetLine: Stop asking for the answer. It isn't coming from there.

cells.tense: A picture is forming in your hands and you have not yet called it yours.
cells.act: do the small practice again, alone, today
cells.ask: Go back to the one plain practice you keep leaving, alone, today — same thing, same way, no additions, nobody watching — and finish it once.
cells.core: You've been reading your life as mostly unchosen. The images turning up in what you make, in what you keep, in what you steer around, are already shaping which door you take. You discuss them the way you'd discuss the forecast. They're not that. They're yours, made by your own hands. And the clearing you do when you let something go is itself one of the pictures you're not counting. Putting it back isn't theory-first. Take up the plain version of the practice you already do, the one you used to do without showing anyone. Do it again, alone, small. The picture you're standing under was made by you, and the making is still happening.
cells.sheetLine: Do the plain practice again, alone, and finish it once.
